canonical_statement: The study aimed to evaluate whether LLM coding agents can perform open-ended hypothesis testing with statistically valid p-values and conclusions.
The study aimed to train an open-weight agent, Fisher-R1, for rigorous hypothesis testing using synthetic executable tasks and reinforcement learning with verified statistical rewards.
P-Bench presents each task as a scientific question, a CSV dataset, and a data description without prescribing the statistical method.
P-Bench requires the agent to return a selected statistical method, a p-value, and a reject/fail-to-reject decision.

outcome.definition: Selected statistical method, p-value, and reject/fail-to-reject decision.

canonical_statement: Agents interact with a logged R execution environment that executes code and returns data summaries, warnings, model outputs, diagnostics, test statistics, and p-values.
P-Bench answer keys are derived from logged execution of canonical reference analyses rather than transcribed p-values from paper text.
The P-Bench construction pipeline reproduces the reference analysis, filters unreproducible analyses, grounds claims in execution logs, and packages self-contained tasks with structured answer keys.

Statistics- and biostatistics-trained reviewers independently audit finalized P-Bench tasks for alignment among the request, released data subset, and answer key; failed tasks are repaired or removed.
P-Bench contains 425 verified open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks split into 203 Easy tasks and 222 Hard tasks.
A P-Bench task is classified as Hard when its reference method requires careful specification/assumption checking or it contains an adversarial data-quality perturbation.
P-Bench spans 17 hypothesis-testing method categories, and no single category exceeds 19% of the benchmark.
P-Bench tasks span economics, biology, and medicine and include randomized experiments and observational studies.

population.label: P-Bench tasks across economics, biology, and medicine

canonical_statement: P-Bench includes adversarial data-quality and assumption-checking traps such as outliers, heteroskedasticity, and clustered observations.
Synthetic training tasks are generated with executable data-generating processes, known target analyses, and programmatically checkable answer keys; P-Bench is kept out of the training set.
The synthetic task taxonomy combines statistical method, domain scenario, sample size, effect size, prompt style, and random seed as independent factors.
The full synthetic training corpus contains 8,642 tasks with balanced coverage.

The SFT teacher generated 4,611 analysis trajectories using Claude-Sonnet-4.6, following a five-step workflow of basic EDA, detailed EDA, assumption checking, method selection/analysis, and conclusion.
Automatic quality control retained 3,851 of 4,611 teacher trajectories for SFT, approximately 83.5%.

SFT quality control requires a valid multi-turn trace, a parseable conclusion matching the ground-truth decision, and when a p-value is reported, significance agreement at alpha=0.05 within one order of magnitude of the key.
Fisher-R1 reinforcement learning uses DAPO initialized from the SFT policy, with asymmetric clipping epsilon_low=0.20 and epsilon_high=0.28 and dynamic resampling of reward-degenerate rollout groups.
The Fisher reward is gated by a valid-format indicator and combines p-value closeness and conclusion correctness with weights 0.9 and 0.1, respectively.
P-value closeness is scored after mapping p-values to a two-sided standard-normal z scale, with z values capped at 5 before computing an exponential closeness reward.
The RL reward does not include an explicit method-correctness term; method choice is assessed indirectly through agreement of the resulting p-value with the canonical analysis.
Evaluation uses three independent rollouts per P-Bench task for each model.
Raw correctness requires the final reject/fail-to-reject decision to match the ground-truth decision at alpha=0.05; unparseable rollouts are incorrect.

outcome.definition: Correct reject/fail-to-reject decision at alpha=0.05; unparseable rollouts count as incorrect.

canonical_statement: Strict correctness requires Raw correctness plus absolute z-space p-value error below 0.5.

outcome.definition: Raw correctness plus |z(p_hat)-z(p*)| < 0.5.

canonical_statement: pass@1 is the average per-trial success rate across the three trials, whereas pass@3 marks a task solved if any of its three trials succeeds.

canonical_statement: The SFT warm-start combined with DAPO achieved the best score on every ablation metric, while DAPO-only and SFT-only variants were inferior.
The memorization check embeds each P-Bench prompt and computes its mean cosine similarity to the top five nearest training prompts using text-embedding-3-small.
Evaluation-to-training similarities lay below the high-similarity train-to-train band, and the authors report no near-duplicate P-Bench counterparts in the RL corpus.
The similarity analysis does not constitute an exhaustive contamination audit because it relies on semantic embeddings of prompts rather than full datasets, code, or external pretraining corpora.
The authors conclude that current frontier LLM agents still lack reliable statistical reasoning for open-ended hypothesis testing and that targeted verified-reward training can improve performance.
P-Bench evaluates a single hypothesis test per task and does not evaluate multi-test pipelines with multiple-comparison correction.
The authors caution that reliable statistical agents could lend false legitimacy to weak claims and should not substitute for human statistical review.
The authors state that P-Bench and Fisher-R1 are released as evaluation and oversight tools.

The P-Bench data-curation agent extracts claims, reproduces analyses in a clean environment, reads inferential values from execution logs, discards ambiguous or inconsistent cases, and sends retained cases for expert review.
For synthetic tasks, each answer key records the output of the canonical method on the simulated dataset rather than the true generative parameter.

The synthetic generator uses 27 statistical methods, 5–7 domain scenarios per method, four method-specific sample-size levels, three effect-size regimes, hint/non-hint prompts, and three deterministic seeds.
The synthetic corpus adds 60 perturbed regression-task variants involving missing values or extreme/invalid outliers, with answer keys computed using a standard handling protocol.

SFT uses 3 epochs, learning rate 1e-5, cosine scheduling, 0.1 warmup ratio, batch size 16, and 8192-token cutoff; RL uses 1 epoch, learning rate 1e-6, batch size 16, 2048-token prompts, and 4096-token responses.
RL rollouts use temperature 0.7, top-p 1.0, and group size 8; inference uses temperature 0.3, top-p 0.9, and batch size 10.
All training and evaluation runs were conducted on a single node with NVIDIA H200 GPUs with 141 GB HBM each; the 14B RL run completed in about 36 hours.
